Content:
Suppose that [MATH: \angle{AOB}] shown above represents [MATH: \dfrac{1}{10}] of a full turn. How can we find the measure of this angle?

Content:
The angle [MATH: \angle AOB] represents one-tenth of a full turn. Since a full turn has a measure of [MATH: 360^\circ,] the measure of [MATH: \angle AOB] is one-tenth of [MATH: 360^\circ.]

Content:
Therefore, we can express the degree measure of [MATH: \angle{AOB}] as follows:

Content:
[MATH: (1)/(10) × 360^{∘}|=; (1 × 360^{∘})/(10)|=; (360^{∘})/(10)]

Content:
It's common to write the fraction in parentheses and place the degree symbol outside, as follows:

Content:
[MATH: ((360)/(10))^{∘}]

Content:
Finally, we simplify this fraction by expressing it as a division.

Content:
[MATH: (360)/(10)|=; 360 ÷ 10; 360; 36]

Content:
Therefore, we conclude that the measure of [MATH: \angle AOB] is [MATH: 36^\circ.]
